classification.difficultyReason: Combines independent-event trees, expected frequency, a two-way outcome table and complementary probability.

content.prompt: I have a 6-sided die and a coin.

children.label: a
children.prompt: You roll the die twice. Draw a tree diagram to calculate the probability you get exactly 1 six.

answer.worked:
Let $S$ denote a six and $N$ denote a number other than six.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{exactly 1 six})&=P(SN)+P(NS)\\P(\text{exactly 1 six})&=\frac16\times\frac56+\frac56\times\frac16\\P(\text{exactly 1 six})&=\frac{10}{36}\\P(\text{exactly 1 six})&=\frac5{18}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored two-stage probability tree completing the requested student drawing; no tree is supplied in the question.
spec.mathematics: Each independent roll has P(S)=1/6 and P(N)=5/6. Ordered outcomes are SS, SN, NS and NN; exactly one six occurs on SN and NS.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If you roll the die 72 times, how many sixes would you expect to get?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Expected number of sixes}&=72\times\frac16\\\text{Expected number of sixes}&=12\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt:
You flip the coin and roll the die.
Draw a two-way table to find the probability you get tails and an even number.

inlines.text: The favourable outcomes are T2, T4 and T6, among 12 equally likely outcomes.

children.label: d
children.prompt:
You flip the coin 3 times.
List all the possible outcomes and find the probability of getting at least 1 head.

answer.short: $HHH,\ HHT,\ HTH,\ HTT,\ THH,\ THT,\ TTH,\ TTT$; $P(\text{at least 1 head})=\frac78$.
answer.worked:
The ordered outcomes are $HHH,\ HHT,\ HTH,\ HTT,\ THH,\ THT,\ TTH,\ TTT$. Seven of the eight equally likely outcomes contain at least one head.
$$P(\text{at least 1 head})=\frac78.$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: How could you use complementary events to calculate the answer to part d quickly?

answer.worked:
The complement of at least one head is no heads, which means all tails.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least 1 head})&=1-P(\text{no heads})\\P(\text{at least 1 head})&=1-P(\text{all tails})\\P(\text{at least 1 head})&=1-\frac12\times\frac12\times\frac12\\P(\text{at least 1 head})&=\frac78\end{align*}$$
